text:
maya: Heads-up — I'm trying to wire per-route quota + rollout state through the gateway so the Console can show accurate bucket usage during canaries. Current plan: inject runtime metadata on the request and have downstream services echo it for telemetry. Thoughts?

simon: echoing metadata works but we need a stable schema. headers are easiest (X-RW-Route, X-RW-QuotaPolicy), but protobufs + dynamic metadata would be cleaner long-term.

anita: Envoy stats/dynamic metadata can carry route info without touching every service. You can access it in filters and emit a span tag. downside: harder to surface in our existing per-token cost pipeline.

maya: yeah, Console expects a route identifier in tracing and in the usage pipeline so cost attribution ends up per-route/model. If we put it in a header, it flows through existing logs and ELT.

tom: concern: headers are easy to spoof if we accept them at edge. We need to ensure gateway is authoritative — gateway should set X-RW-Route based on the routing table (not accept client-supplied). Also we need signed route tokens for internal invocations.

simon: agreed. gateway MUST canonicalize. proposal: gateway strips any incoming X-RW-* headers and sets its own. It also sets X-RW-Route-Version for rollout buckets.

anita: rollout UX ask: Console needs both current canonical route and the rollout label (canary/A/B) to join metrics. We also want percent-exposure telemetry. Can the gateway emit both route id and rollout tag into traces and logs?

maya: yes — gateway will emit two fields. Thinking about telemetry schema: route_id, rollout_id, rollout_pct, quota_policy. Example header form we can use internally:

```
X-RW-Route: models/text-gen/v2
X-RW-Rollout: rollout-2026-03-phi
X-RW-Rollout-Pct: 10
X-RW-Quota: tenant:100k/day
```

maya: those then get picked up by our log forwarder and perf pipeline.

tom: For proto-first teams, can we mirror this in metadata proto so services that only talk gRPC don't need to parse headers? Something like: `RouteMeta` in the `common` proto that gets set by gateway.

simon: yes — add a top-level google.protobuf.Struct field or a dedicated RouteMeta message on the RPC envelope. But that requires touching a lot of in-process clients. header fallback is lower friction.

anita: From metrics side, we need a stable join key. route_id + rollout_id works. Also need the gateway to emit percentage and sample buckets so we can compute exposure in Console (not just infer from count). If we only rely on request counts we might miss retries/backfills.

maya: operationally, we also want a per-request flag for "quota-charged" vs "cache-hit" so the billing pipeline accurately attributes tokens. Gateway should annotate when response came from KV cache vs served raw. 

simon: agree — X-RW-Cache-Hit: true/false or `x-rw-kv-hit`. that helps Optimize and billing.

tom: security note: route metadata may contain tenant IDs. If route_id leaks, is that a problem? probably okay internally but we should avoid exposing tenant in public logs. gateway should redact before any public export.

maya: yep — gateway will redact tenant in any external telemetry and send tenant hashes only. Console will map hashes to tenants internally.

anita: rollout UI: we want to show per-rollout latency, error rate, and cost per 1k tokens. So telemetry must include token_count (response_tokens, request_tokens) per request. Any objections?

simon: token_count is already emitted in runtime; gate can attach it or downstream can. But we need schema: `tokens_in`, `tokens_out` on the trace/span.

maya: final question: proto vs headers parity — do we implement headers now and start a RFC for proto envelope migration?

tom: do headers for fast rollout. start RFC for RouteMeta proto that will be enforced by SDKs next quarter. Add a console flag to prefer proto metadata when present. :thumbsup:

devx-bot: Reminder: runbook template created: https://go.redwood/infra-rollout-telemetry (created by devx-bot)

anita: timeline: gateway header injection change -> telemetry pipeline mapping -> Console adds rollout dimension. Canaries with 5/10/25% exposed once pipeline validated. I'll own dashboard wiring.

maya: thanks all. I'll put up a small patch in gateway that strips incoming X-RW-* headers and injects canonical ones. Will also include Envoy dynamic metadata for services that opt-in.

simon: ping me for the proto sketch if you want me to draft RouteMeta. I'll include proto examples and envoy filter bits.

maya: perfect — we'll sync in the infra standup tomorrow. :rocket:
